/audio/threadit/kokoro-heart/threadit-01.speechText: entangled. Definition: Caught or twisted in something, making movement difficult. In this passage, a fox’s tail becomes entangled in a hedge.
brush. Definition: Another definition: a fox’s bushy tail. In this passage, the fox claims that his brush slows him down.
jeers. Definition: Mocking remarks or sounds meant to ridicule someone. In this passage, the foxes answer his advice with jeers.

/audio/threadit/kokoro-heart/threadit-02.speechText: diffidence. Definition: Lack of certainty or confidence in expressing oneself. In this passage, Franklin expresses his opinions with modest diffidence.
inculcate. Definition: Teach or impress an idea through repeated emphasis. In this passage, Franklin finds a modest tone helps him inculcate his opinions.
dogmatical. Definition: Stating opinions as unquestionably true. In this passage, a dogmatical tone can keep listeners from considering an idea.

/audio/threadit/kokoro-heart/threadit-03.speechText: feud. Definition: A bitter conflict between families or groups that continues over time. In this passage, Buck fights because of an old family feud.
lawsuit. Definition: A dispute brought before a court for a legal decision. In this passage, a lawsuit failed to end the families’ dispute.
row. Definition: Another definition: a noisy argument or quarrel. Here, pronounced to rhyme with “cow.”. In this passage, Buck cannot explain what the original row was about.

/audio/threadit/kokoro-heart/threadit-04.speechText: emancipation. Definition: The act of freeing someone from slavery or control. In this passage, the dialogue ends in the enslaved man's emancipation.
unabated. Definition: Continuing without becoming weaker or less intense. In this passage, Douglass rereads the works with unabated interest.
vindication. Definition: A strong defense showing that a claim, cause, or right is justified. In this passage, Sheridan offers a vindication of human rights.

/audio/threadit/kokoro-heart/threadit-05.speechText: reserve. Definition: Restraint in expressing thoughts or feelings. In this passage, Henry wants to speak without reserve.
magnitude. Definition: Great size, importance, or seriousness. In this passage, the issue’s magnitude calls for open debate.
revere. Definition: Regard with deep respect or reverence. In this passage, Henry says he reveres heaven above earthly kings.

/audio/threadit/kokoro-heart/threadit-06.speechText: indictment. Definition: A formal accusation that someone has committed a crime. In this passage, Anthony stands under indictment for voting.
posterity. Definition: People of future generations. In this passage, the Constitution promises liberty to posterity.
mockery. Definition: An act that makes something seem false, empty, or ridiculous. In this passage, Anthony calls liberty without a vote a mockery.

/audio/threadit/kokoro-heart/threadit-07.speechText: dissipating. Definition: Causing energy or attention to be scattered or wasted. In this passage, too much company can feel wearisome and dissipating.
intervene. Definition: To come or exist between two things. In this passage, miles may intervene without deciding whether a person is lonely.
suffice. Definition: To be enough for a particular purpose. In this passage, less frequent contact may suffice for important communication.

/audio/threadit/kokoro-heart/threadit-08.speechText: discerning. Definition: Able to notice differences and judge carefully. In this passage, a discerning observer may see wisdom where others see madness.
assent. Definition: Agree or express approval. In this passage, those who assent are treated as sensible.
demur. Definition: Raise an objection or express disagreement. In this passage, those who demur are treated as dangerous.

/audio/threadit/kokoro-heart/threadit-09.speechText: contrary. Definition: Opposite or opposed to something. In this passage, one person may hold a contrary opinion.
dissent. Definition: Disagree with an opinion or decision. In this passage, people who dissent also lose when discussion is silenced.
stifle. Definition: Prevent something from being expressed or developing. In this passage, silencing an opinion can stifle useful discussion.
